key_insight: This paper shows how to turn standard neural network architectures into neural operators that work on continuous function spaces, rather than fixed grids. The result is models that can learn scientific dynamics more reliably and stay accurate across different discretization resolutions.
problem_solved: Many neural networks perform well only on the specific grid or resolution they were trained on, making them brittle for scientific simulations that change resolution. This work addresses the challenge of building models that generalize across discretizations and learn directly from continuous data.
method: Extend popular neural architectures into operator-learning frameworks that map between functions instead of finite arrays.
Design the models to be discretization-agnostic, so the same learned operator can be evaluated at different resolutions.
Adapt neural network components to continuous scientific settings, improving transfer from training data to simulation settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a principled path from conventional deep learning models to more reliable scientific surrogates and simulators. It can reduce retraining costs and improve robustness when deploying models across meshes, grids, or sensor densities.

paper_title: Principled approaches for extending neural architectures to function spaces for operator learning
